claims.text: The studied alloy has composition Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17.
The as-deposited thin films and nanoribbons are amorphous.
The as-deposited material exhibits a single cubic-type short-range order.
The as-deposited surface has Rq approximately 0.79 nm and Ra approximately 0.63 nm.
Annealing at 700 K induces short-range atomic reordering without long-range crystallization.
Annealing at 700 K relaxes fabrication-induced internal stresses.
Short-range atomic reordering and internal-strain relaxation reduce local domain-pinning barriers.
Short-range atomic reordering and internal-strain relaxation improve collective ferromagnetic exchange interactions.
The annealing-induced changes enhance the effective ferromagnetic network and ferromagnetic volume fraction.
The enhanced ferromagnetic network increases spin-entropy variation and the magnetocaloric response.
Annealing reduces magnetic hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Elastic longitudinal tensile strain further stabilizes the ordered magnetic configuration through magnetoelastic coupling, particularly above 100 K.
The strain-mediated magnetic enhancement preserves in-plane isotropy.
The as-deposited 1 µm-spaced nanoribbon array has a maximum −ΔSM of approximately 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K for ΔH = 50 kOe.
Applying elastic longitudinal tensile strain strengthens the magnetic response above 100 K.
Applying elastic longitudinal tensile strain does not shift the magnetic-cluster blocking peak.
Increasing nanoribbon spacing from 1 µm to 2 µm suppresses coupling-related in-plane anisotropy.
The magnetocaloric response is primarily active between 40 K and 200 K.
Full crystallization occurs near 1000 K.
Longitudinal tensile strains from 0% to 2% remain within the elastic regime for these nanoribbons.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as a '580 K annealing' performed 'at 700 K,' giving two incompatible annealing temperatures without explaining whether 580 K is a hold, onset, or typographical error.

The response is repeatedly framed as occurring during low-applied-field cycles, but the quantitative baseline and proposed measurements use fields up to 50 kOe (about 5 T), which is not ordinarily a low applied field.
